title: Idioms & Phrases: Meaning, Usage, Context and Exam Practice
description: Established idioms across 10 semantic domains: Success & Failure, Effort & Work, Secrets & Communication, Emotions & Behaviour, Money & Resources, Time & Frequency, Relationships & Conflict, Decisions & Consequences, Honesty & Judgment, along with literal vs figurative distinctions, grammatical variation, and High Court competitive exam traps ko systematically master karein.
learningObjectives: Idioms aur idiomatic phrases ke figurative vs literal meaning ke fundamental difference ko accurately define karein
Sentence context aur subtle tone clues ka use karke idiom ka intended meaning decode karein
Success, failure, achievement, aur recovery se jude high-frequency idioms ko master karein
Effort, diligence, endurance, aur shortcuts se jude idioms ke precise boundaries samjhein
Secrets, disclosure, misinformation, aur communication styles se jude idioms ko distinguish karein
Emotions, psychological states, temper, aur personality traits se jude idioms ko accurately identify karein
Money, valuation, expenditure, aur scarcity se jude idioms ko proverbs se differentiate karein
Time, speed, delay, deadlines, aur frequency expressions ke exact intervals ko calculate karein
Interpersonal relationships, agreement, reconciliation, aur conflict ke idioms ko recognize karein
Decision making, risk assessment, delay, hesitation, aur accountability expressions ko master karein
Idiom structure mein fixed vs flexible elements (tense changes, pronoun variation, possessive concord) ko correctly apply karein
Idioms, proverbs, clichés, aur phrasal verbs ke beech clear structural aur conceptual distinction karein
8-Step Systematic Idiom Solving Protocol apply karke competitive exam MCQs mein 100% accuracy achieve karein

included: Core Idiom Nature: Figurative vs literal meaning, conventional phraseology, and non-compositionality

Success, Failure & Achievement: hit the jackpot, make it, get off the ground, go places, come out on top, miss the mark, fall flat, back to square one, draw a blank, come up short, rise to the occasion, get the ball rolling, pull it off, be on the right track, learn the hard way

Effort, Work & Determination: burn the midnight oil, go the extra mile, leave no stone unturned, keep at it, put one's best foot forward, pull one's weight, get down to business, be snowed under, work against the clock, go back to the drawing board, bite the bullet, keep one's nose to the grindstone, give it one's best shot, on the home stretch, cut corners

Secrets, Communication & Information: spill the beans, let the cat out of the bag, keep under wraps, beat around the bush, get straight to the point, read between the lines, hear through the grapevine, keep someone in the loop, get the wrong end of the stick, put words in someone's mouth, speak one's mind, have a change of heart, at the tip of one's tongue, word of mouth, clear the air

Emotions, Behaviour & Personality: lose one's temper, keep one's cool, down in the dumps, on cloud nine, butterflies in one's stomach, get cold feet, a blessing in disguise, add fuel to the fire, make a mountain out of a molehill, chip on one's shoulder, wear one's heart on one's sleeve, over the moon, keep one's chin up, get on someone's nerves, drive someone up the wall, take to heart, mixed feelings, a bitter pill to swallow

Money, Value & Resources: cost an arm and a leg, break the bank, make ends meet, live from hand to mouth, save for a rainy day, worth one's weight in gold, money doesn't grow on trees, tighten one's belt, bring home the bacon, pay through the nose, on a shoestring, a penny saved is a penny earned

Time & Frequency: once in a blue moon, in the nick of time, around the clock, at the eleventh hour, time flies, ahead of one's time, in no time, behind the times, better late than never, call it a day, kill time, from time to time, against the clock, in the long run, at the drop of a hat

Relationships, Cooperation & Conflict: see eye to eye, get along with, bury the hatchet, break the ice, extend an olive branch, a shoulder to cry on, through thick and thin, know someone inside out, give the cold shoulder, make up, get on like a house on fire, at loggerheads, two peas in a pod, lend a hand, pull together

Decisions, Risk & Consequences: jump the gun, play it by ear, take the plunge, in two minds, sit on the fence, a close call, the last straw, cross that bridge when you come to it, the ball is in your court, double-edged sword, open a can of worms, face the music, take a calculated risk, put all eggs in one basket, look before you leap, cut to the chase

Honesty, Mistakes & Judgment: turn a blind eye, call a spade a spade, tip of the iceberg, let sleeping dogs lie, jump to conclusions, put one's foot in one's mouth, make a fool of oneself, pot calling the kettle black, by the book, get away with murder, head in the clouds, not see the forest for the trees, storm in a teacup, bite off more than one can chew, the writing is on the wall
Grammatical Structure & Flexibility: Tense shifts, subject-possessive concord ('keep one's cool' -> 'kept his cool'), fixed article retention, and immutable expressions
Genre Discrimination: Idioms vs Proverbs vs Clichés vs Phrasal Verbs
8-Step Systematic Contextual Elimination & Verification Protocol for High Court Examination
excluded: Broad multi-word phrasal verb particle transformations (covered in dedicated grammar lessons)
Single-word substitutions and Greek/Latin root morphology (covered in Lesson 17)
Direct synonym/antonym pair matching without idiomatic phrasing (covered in Lesson 16)
Affixation and morphological prefixes/suffixes (covered in Lesson 18)
